explanation: Upper 90% acceptability limit of the NBC 2016 adaptive model for naturally ventilated (NV) Indian residential buildings. Neutral operative temperature is Tn = 0.54 * Trm + 12.83 °C.
text: Upper 90% acceptability limit of the NBC 2016 adaptive model for naturally ventilated (NV) Indian residential buildings. Neutral operative temperature is Tn = 0.54 * Trm + 12.83 °C.
application: Evaluate indoor operative temperature compliance for naturally ventilated homes in cooling-dominated seasons.

explanation: Upper 90% acceptability limit of the NBC 2016 adaptive model for mixed-mode (MM) Indian residential buildings. Neutral operative temperature is Tn = 0.28 * Trm + 17.87 °C.
text: Upper 90% acceptability limit of the NBC 2016 adaptive model for mixed-mode (MM) Indian residential buildings. Neutral operative temperature is Tn = 0.28 * Trm + 17.87 °C.
application: Evaluate indoor operative temperature for mixed-mode buildings using hybrid fan and natural ventilation.

explanation: Observed neutral and acceptable comfort temperature bands in Indian field studies across Hyderabad, Jaipur, Chandigarh, and Ahmedabad.
text: Observed neutral and acceptable comfort temperature bands in Indian field studies across Hyderabad, Jaipur, Chandigarh, and Ahmedabad.
application: Field-study benchmark check for composite and hot-dry climates.

rule_or_threshold: Air speed < 0.5 m/s when Tin > neutral + 2.0 °C
explanation: Indoor air speed of 0.5 - 1.5 m/s increases convective and evaporative heat loss from occupants, offsetting higher indoor air temperatures by 3.0 - 5.0 °C.
text: Indoor air speed of 0.5 - 1.5 m/s increases convective and evaporative heat loss from occupants, offsetting higher indoor air temperatures by 3.0 - 5.0 °C.
application: Determine if elevated air speed (ceiling fans or natural breeze) can restore thermal comfort.

rule_or_threshold: Operable window / louver opening area < 20% of floor area
explanation: Adequate natural ventilation and cross-ventilation in cooling-dominated Indian climates requires an operable opening area of at least 20% of the room floor area.
text: Adequate natural ventilation and cross-ventilation in cooling-dominated Indian climates requires an operable opening area of at least 20% of the room floor area.
application: Check window and aperture sizing for cross-ventilation adequacy.

rule_or_threshold: For roof slope < 20°: initial solar reflectance < 0.60 or thermal emittance < 0.90
explanation: To qualify as an effective cool roof under Indian prescriptive standards, low-slope roofs (<20°) must have high solar reflectance (>= 0.60) and high thermal emittance (>= 0.90).
application: Evaluate roof surface optical properties and cool-roof qualification.

rule_or_threshold: Roof insulation R < 3.5 m²·K/W for 24-hour occupancy in hot-dry/warm-humid/composite climates
explanation: Prescribed minimum thermal resistance for roof insulation alone in cooling-dominated residential buildings to prevent conductive solar heat flux.
application: Verify envelope insulation resistance against code prescriptions.

rule_or_threshold: Indoor temperature reduction ΔT < 1.5 °C under peak summer conditions
explanation: Documented performance benchmark from TARU field demonstrations: effective cool-roof treatments produce measured indoor temperature reductions of 1.5 - 6.0 °C versus bare RCC or GI roofs.
application: Check effectiveness of cool-roof treatments against field-measured benchmarks.
source: TARU-2015, all technology case studies (Indore, Surat)

rule_or_threshold: High relative humidity suppressing wet-bulb depression
explanation: High ambient relative humidity reduces evaporative skin cooling and impairs passive direct evaporative cooling strategies, requiring elevated air speeds for comfort.
application: Assess humidity-driven thermal discomfort and evaporative cooling limitations.

explanation: High-reflectance solar reflective paint applied on roof exterior. Low initial cost, rapid application, achieves 2-4 °C indoor cooling in summer.
application: Recommend as top-ranked cost-effective cool-roof intervention for RCC and sheet roofs.

explanation: Elevated treated bamboo slat trellis mounted above the roof deck with an air gap. Blocks 80-90% direct solar radiation while allowing convective airflow underneath.
application: Recommend for lightweight roofs, low-income shelters, and roof-gardens.

explanation: Hollow terracotta clay tiles with internal air cavities topped with broken china mosaic. Durable, permanent, provides thermal insulation + solar reflectance.
application: Recommend for permanent RCC residential roofs requiring long service life.

explanation: Inverted modular earthen pots laid over the roof deck covered with screed. Trapped air cavity acts as lightweight thermal insulation.
application: Recommend as low-cost intermediate-mass roof thermal barrier.

rule_or_threshold: High solar radiation + Low roof SRI + No insulation -> High roof surface temp -> Conductive flux -> Elevated MRT & indoor air temp -> Thermal discomfort
explanation: Uninsulated dark roof decks absorb up to 80-90% incident solar energy, raising interior ceiling surface temperatures up to 45-50 °C and driving severe top-floor overheating.
application: Diagnose root cause of top-floor and single-story daytime thermal distress.

rule_or_threshold: Opening area < 20% + No opposite openings -> Low air velocity (<0.2 m/s) -> Suppressed convective/evaporative cooling -> Discomfort at moderate temperatures
explanation: Inadequate aperture sizing and absence of cross-ventilation prevent indoor air movement, causing heat trapping and physiological sweat stagnation.
application: Diagnose ventilation bottlenecks in naturally ventilated spaces.

rule_or_threshold: Stack exhaust exit preferably one floor above top floor living zone; double-skin ventilated roof cavity removes trapped solar heat
explanation: Natural roof ventilation, ridge ventilators, and double-roof cavities allow heated buoyant air under the roof to escape before transferring heat downward into the living space, vital in hot-humid and warm climates.
text: Natural roof ventilation, ridge ventilators, and double-roof cavities allow heated buoyant air under the roof to escape before transferring heat downward into the living space, vital in hot-humid and warm climates.
application: Design of naturally ventilated roof monitors, ventilated attics, and stack exhausts.

rule_or_threshold: High thermal mass dampens diurnal swings; night ventilation flushes stored daytime heat
explanation: In climates with large diurnal temperature swings (Hot & Dry and Composite), high-mass walls and roofs absorb daytime heat and release it during cooler night hours, which is purged via night ventilation.
text: In climates with large diurnal temperature swings (Hot & Dry and Composite), high-mass walls and roofs absorb daytime heat and release it during cooler night hours, which is purged via night ventilation.
application: Passive cooling in hot-dry and composite zones using night purge cycles.
